title: Everyday regression gate: the right food, a plausible amount, or a safe refusal
rules: Each case says what SHOULD happen (behavior log / suggest / flag), not what happens today.

Outcomes: correct (the right foods and, where a range is given, the right amount; an amount marked assumption must be visibly labelled as an assumption); safely uncertain (nothing wrong logged; a food is listed unmatched instead of logged); incorrect (a wrong food, an amount out of range, an assumed amount not labelled, a food logged where it should be asked about, a lost user amount, or a food silently dropped).

Measures (not interchangeable): katori = 200 ml (ICMR-NIN 2024 Annexure I). Bowl = 200 ml and glass = 250 ml, both PROVISIONAL owner assumptions that a logged item must label. A bare 'cup' is always the USDA standard cup (236.6 ml; the food's own USDA '1 cup' portion). The NIN serving cup (200 ml) is used only by the named NIN plate-serving assumptions, never for a bare 'cup'.

Volume to grams only through the food's own cited density (its USDA cup portion). Recipe portions that are importer or authoring defaults (every INDB recipe's '1 cup = 240 g'; the lassi and kheer recipes) are not cited densities. No cited density: the case expects flag.

Plates: no universal plate weight, and no source defines a plate. Only plain cooked rice has an assumption: NIN's 1-cup (200 ml) serving quantity for rice, whose calories agree with USDA cooked rice, logged as a labelled Nutrikit assumption. Every other plate expects flag, including idli and upma, whose NIN quantities disagree with USDA's weight or energy for the same food (owner decision 2026-11-19).

Sweets: published piece ranges (rasgulla 15.7-43.4 g, gulab jamun 24.2-44.4 g) are plausibility bounds only, never defaults: an unsupported piece count expects flag. User-given grams are used as given.
Food patterns are exact, reviewed catalog names (anchored); a broad pattern must not hide a wrong match. Every 'log' pattern must match a catalog food (checked at build).
Known incorrect cases are listed in test/everyday-gate.test.mjs with their finding.

A case marked uncertain is one whose best achievable outcome is safely uncertain: when the app behaves exactly as expected (logs what it should and asks about the rest), it scores safely uncertain, never correct automatic logging.
